# My Cotton Plan This Year

Alright, let me think about this year's cotton. I've been doing this for ten years on the same 1.5 mu, so I mostly know what works. My wife and I handle the field — the older kids help on weekends and during picking season, and my younger brother comes back from his factory job to help when we need extra hands.

**First thing — the plot is small.** Only 1.5 mu. I'm not going to get rich off this land. The cash from the factory work matters more than what I make from cotton. But cotton is what our family has always grown on this plot, and the western part of Quzhou is cotton country. The land suits it, and I know how to manage it. Switching to wheat-maize would mean buying a planter or hiring one twice a year, and on 1.5 mu it's not worth it.

**Planting.** I'll plant around April 20-25, once the soil warms up. I always lay plastic mulch first — almost everyone around here does. The mulch keeps the soil warm early and cuts down on weeds, which saves me herbicide spray later. I buy seed from the agri-supply shop in town, usually a hybrid variety — last year I used Guoxin 6 and it did okay, so I'll probably stick with that unless the shop owner pushes something new that my cousin vouches for.

**Fertilizer.** My usual plan: about 40 kg of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) as base before I lay the mulch, then topdress about 10 kg of urea at the budding stage in late June. That works out to maybe 10 kg of N per mu total, plus P and K from the compound. Some of the bigger cotton growers down the road push harder — 18-20 kg N — but on my small plot I don't want to waste money, and too much nitrogen makes the plant grow tall with fewer bolls. My father taught me that. Middle of the road is safe.

**Irrigation.** I've got well access, which is lucky — a lot of folks in the village share wells and have to wait their turn. I'll probably irrigate twice: once around flowering in July if it hasn't rained enough, and once during boll formation in August. Pumping costs money — diesel isn't cheap — so I don't irrigate unless the plants really need it. If it rains well in summer I might skip one.

**Pesticide — this is the big one for cotton.** Bollworms, aphids, spider mites. I'll spray 4-5 times through the season. I watch the plants and spray when I see the pests, not on a fixed schedule. I use whatever the shop has — usually a pyrethroid mix. I also do one herbicide spray before planting, even with the mulch, just to be safe.

**Labor.** Family only. My wife does most of the weeding and thinning. Picking in September-October is when everyone helps — it takes multiple passes, maybe 3-4 picks, and that's when my brother comes back. No hired labor on 1.5 mu; it doesn't pay.

**Yield.** Last year I got about 260 kg/mu of lint cotton. The year before, closer to 240 because of that dry spell in August. I'm hoping for around 260 this year if weather cooperates.
